objective: Proof and census. On the connected cubic substrates (all 60 with up to 8 points): the knot fails (under some signing) exactly on Pfaffian substrates and every failure is global (minimal); signed parity, and so blurred parity, fails exactly on substrates with an even number of perfect matchings and no failure is ever global (three is odd, so no dependency uses every line); signed Z3 fails on every substrate (three is zero mod 3) and its failures are global exactly when the Z3-corank is 1. Blurred Z3 on corank-1 substrates: global, recognisable failures, easy counts with a line removed (three solutions), hard counts in general, cycle-like composition: the first law that both selects and composes, at four values; its selection is linear (corank), the knot's is sign-nonsingular.
status: Proved by BEYOND-TWO-20261101-001C-P001: on connected cubic substrates the knot fails exactly on Pfaffian ones, always globally; parity (and blurred parity) exactly where the number of perfect matchings is even, never globally (three is odd); Z3 (and blurred Z3) on every substrate, globally exactly at Z3-corank 1 (3 = 0 mod 3); all 60 substrates with up to 8 points checked (8 Pfaffian, 38 even, 24 corank 1). Blurred Z3 on corank-1 substrates both selects (global, recognisable failures; three solutions after removing a line, so easy in return; #P-complete in general) and composes like cycles: a bridge at four values; but its selected spaces are rigid (only ties after removing a line), while the knot's can keep a knot (Fano)
title: Which substrates a law fails on, and whether globally
